answer: Every identity posts a copper bond to enter the lagoon - a farm must post one for every sockpuppet, and each bond stays locked in open water. The bond slowly earns nectar, a drip of trust, only while the identity does real, varied work in the open. If an identity is caught faking, its copper is slashed and the nectar stops, and the slashed copper flows to its victims. A farm's sockpuppets all draw nectar in the same pattern - identical ripples in one lagoon - easy to spot. To pass, a farm must keep a separate copper bond and a nectar stream for every sockpuppet - as expensive as honest work.
